AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: To evaluate phenotypic differences among familial and non-familial JOAG patients.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: First degree relatives of unrelated JOAG patients were screened for glaucoma and ocular hypertension. JOAG probands were grouped as familial or non-familial and phenotypic differences in terms of age of onset, gender, baseline untreated IOP, presence angle dysgenesis, and refractive error was compared between the two groups.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Out of 368 unrelated JOAG patients, 134 in whom all first degree relatives had been examined were included in the study. The non-familial JOAG (n = 96) had similar age of onset as familial JOAG (n = 38); (p = 0.076) but had greater male preponderance (p = 0.046), and had the higher baseline IOP (p = 0.044) compared to familial JOAG. However, on adjustment using the Bonferroni correction, the observed differences were not found to be significant. Both groups had similar proportion of patients with angle dysgenesis (p = 0.46) and high myopia (p = 0.72).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Non-familial JOAG were not found to be phenotypically different from the familial JOAG patients in this cohort.
